briefing.headline: Harbour Town control the pitch by pressing high and attacking predominantly down the left; Kestrel are being forced wide and struggle to regain territory

working.text: Harbour have dominated territory into the final third, getting 34 entries and 78.2% of the field tilt in their favour.
They press intensely (low PPDA 3.1) and convert that pressure into high wins: 19 regains in the opponent’s third.
Harbour recover the ball very high (mean turnover x = 54.8 m) which sustains their attacking sequences and has produced most of their chances (xG 0.75).

not_working.text: Their press intensity risks fading: a PPDA of 3.1 is very low and is likely to rise if legs tire.
Harbour concentrate entries heavily down their left (70.6% of entries), making their attack predictable against Kestrel’s right.
Despite territorial dominance they still need to convert chances—seven shots produced 0.75 xG, showing good chance creation but a need to maintain efficiency.

predictions.claim: Kavanagh will ask Harbour to protect their left flank to reduce Kestrel’s right-side access.
To manage fatigue, Harbour’s PPDA will rise as they ease the intensity of the press.
Harbour will push to keep territorial control and at least maintain or increase their final-third entries.

working.text: Kestrel have struggled for territory and creation: 44.8% possession and only 0.04 xG reflect a lack of forward momentum.
They favour attacks down the right (58.3% of their channel share), probing Harbour’s left.
Kestrel defend deeper (defensive line ~22.8 m) and win the ball much lower (turnover height 28.8 m), allowing Harbour to operate higher upfield.

not_working.text: Their press is very light (PPDA 11.2), so they rarely disrupt Harbour’s build and concede many high regains (Harbour 19 high wins).
Kestrel’s final-third entries are low (12), and their right-sided bias is being contained by Harbour’s wide pressing.
With a shallow defensive line they’re ceding space between the lines and not recovering possession high enough to threaten.

predictions.claim: Molina will ask Kestrel to defend their right more tightly to cut Harbour’s heavy left-channel access.
To stop Harbour’s high wins, Kestrel will drop a midfielder deeper to reduce high regains against them.
Kestrel will seek more possession by moving players higher to increase their overall possession share.
